scanNote:
10-UNITNING TO'RTINChI BETI (73-bet).

Yuqorida o'ngda 'Stick to the Rules!' va YaShIL yorliqda oq '10'.

CHAP USTUN:
13) 'What rules do taxi drivers in your country have to follow? Tick (✓) the correct column next to each prompt, then use the information in the table to talk about taxi drivers in your country.' SURAT: taksida ko'k ko'ylakli haydovchi o'girilib turibdi, orqada kostyumli yo'lovchi pul uzatmoqda. JADVAL 'TAXI DRIVERS ...' | must | mustn't | don't have to: wear a uniform; switch the meter on; drive carefully; be rude to passengers; carry more than four passengers; have a mobile phone with them. Ko'k qiya: "In my country, taxi drivers don't have to wear a uniform."
• Pushti nuqta va to'q sariq 'Grammar: Can - Be allowed to'. OCh KO'K quti 'Use': • 'We use CAN to ask for or give permission, and CAN'T to refuse permission. "CAN I go out?" "Of course you CAN." I'm afraid you CAN'T enter this room.' • 'We use BE ALLOWED TO to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker. Compare the examples: CAN I play in the garden? (Will you allow me to play in the garden?) AM I ALLOWED TO use the telephone? (What is the rule?)'
14) 'In pairs, use the prompts to act out short dialogues, as in the example.' Ko'k qiya: SA: CAN I park my car here? SB: No, I'm afraid not. You AREN'T ALLOWED TO park here. You HAVE TO park somewhere else.
   (O'NG USTUNDA:) 1 ... I park my car here? (park somewhere else) 2 ... my child come into the hospital? (leave him outside) 3 ... we take photographs in the museum? (leave your cameras in the cloakroom) 4 ... we eat in here? (eat your food outside) 5 ... I wear shorts in this restaurant? (wear a suit and tie) 6 ... I use this telephone? (use the public phone outside)

O'NG USTUN:
• Pushti nuqta va to'q sariq 'Grammar: Had to/didn't have to - Could/couldn't'. OCh KO'K quti 'Use': • 'HAD TO and DIDN'T HAVE TO are the past forms of HAVE TO and DON'T HAVE TO. When my father was a boy, he HAD TO wear shorts to school. Children DIDN'T HAVE TO learn about computers at school twenty years ago.' • 'COULD and COULDN'T are the past forms of CAN and CAN'T. I COULD go to parties when I was 17, but I COULDN'T go on my own; I HAD TO go with my brother.'
15) Kasseta belgisi: qiya 'Mrs Smith is telling her granddaughter about her parents' dinner parties when she and her sister were children.' 'Listen and tick (✓) the correct column. Finally, ask and answer questions in pairs, using Did they have to...?/Could they ...? as in the example.' Ko'k qiya: SA: Did they have to wear their best clothes? SB: Yes, they did. They had to wear their best clothes. BINAFShA JADVAL | could | couldn't | had to | didn't have to: wear best clothes; play piano for guests before dinner; cook; sit at same table as adults; put elbows on table; drink wine like adults; go to bed early; sit in living room with adults after dinner.

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '73'.

sections.title: Grammar: must / mustn't / don't have to
sections.titleUz: Grammatika: must / mustn't / don't have to

exercises.instructionEn: What rules do taxi drivers in your country have to follow? Tick (✓) the correct column next to each prompt, then use the information in the table to talk about taxi drivers in your country.
exercises.instructionUz: Mamlakatingizda taksi haydovchilari qanday qoidalarga rioya qilishi kerak? Har ko'rsatma yoniga to'g'ri ustunga ✓ qo'ying, so'ng jadvaldagi ma'lumotdan foydalanib mamlakatingizdagi taksi haydovchilari haqida gapiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
O'Z MAMLAKATINGIZ HAQIDA -
"to'g'ri" javob yo'q.

KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:
  "In my country, taxi drivers don't
   have to wear a uniform."


UCh USTUN:

  must = ShART (qoida)
  mustn't = TAQIQ
  don't have to = ShART EMAS


EhTIMOLIY JAVOBLAR (O'zbekiston):

  wear a uniform → don't have to
  switch the meter on → must
  drive carefully → must
  be rude to passengers → mustn't
  carry more than four passengers →
     mustn't
  have a mobile phone with them →
     don't have to


⚠ 'TO SWITCH ON':

  = yoqmoq (asbob).
  ⚠ 'the meter' = taksometr.


⚠ 'A PASSENGER':

  = yo'lovchi.
  ⚠ O'qilishi /ˈpæsɪndʒə/.


⚠ 'RUDE TO SB':

  = kimgadir qo'pol.
exercises.exampleEn: In my country, taxi drivers don't have to wear a uniform.
exercises.exampleUz: Mamlakatimda taksi haydovchilari forma kiyishi shart emas.
modelAnswers: In my country, taxi drivers don't have to wear a uniform.
They must switch the meter on.
They mustn't be rude to passengers.
They mustn't carry more than four passengers.
They don't have to have a mobile phone with them.
modelAnswersUz: Mamlakatimda taksi haydovchilari forma kiyishi shart emas.
Ular to'rttadan ortiq yo'lovchi olmasligi shart.
Ularda mobil telefon bo'lishi shart emas.

exercises.explanationUz:
RUXSAT: CAN va BE ALLOWED TO.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  CAN / CAN'T                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  Ruxsat SO'RASh, BERISh, RAD ETISh:
  "Can I go out?" - "Of course you
   can."
  "I'm afraid you can't enter this
   room."
  ⚠ Ruxsat GAPIRUVChIga bog'liq.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  BE ALLOWED TO                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = ruxsat berilgan bo'lmoq.
  ⚠ Ruxsat QOIDAga bog'liq,
  gapiruvchiga EMAS.

  'Can I play in the garden?'
     = Sen menga ruxsat berasanmi?
  'Am I allowed to use the
   telephone?'
     = Qoida bo'yicha mumkinmi?


⚠ ShAKLI:

  am/is/are + allowed to + fe'l
  'You aren't allowed to park here.'
  'Are we allowed to smoke?'


⚠ 'TO ALLOW':

  = ruxsat bermoq.
  ⚠ 'allow sb TO do' (70-bet).


⚠ 'PERMISSION':

  = ruxsat (ot).
  ⚠ 'to ask for permission' = ruxsat
  so'ramoq.

points.en: We use can to ask for or give permission, and can't to refuse permission. "Can I go out?" "Of course you can." I'm afraid you can't enter this room.
points.uz: 'can' ni ruxsat so'rash yoki berish, 'can't' ni rad etish uchun ishlatamiz. "Chiqsam bo'ladimi?" "Albatta." Afsuski, bu xonaga kira olmaysiz.

points.en: We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker.
points.uz: 'be allowed to' ni ruxsat so'rash, berish yoki rad etish uchun ishlatamiz. Lekin ruxsat gapiruvchiga bog'liq emas.

points.en: Can I play in the garden? (Will you allow me to play in the garden?) / Am I allowed to use the telephone? (What is the rule?)
points.uz: Bog'da o'ynasam bo'ladimi? (Sen ruxsat berasanmi?) / Telefondan foydalanishga ruxsat bormi? (Qoida qanday?)

exercises.instructionEn: In pairs, use the prompts to act out short dialogues, as in the example.
exercises.instructionUz: Juftlikda ko'rsatmalardan foydalanib qisqa dialoglar tuzing, namunadagidek.
exercises.explanationUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  SA: Can I park my car here?
  SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't
      allowed to park here. You have
      to park somewhere else.


⚠ QOLIP:

  SA: Can [ega] + fe'l ...?
  SB: No, I'm afraid not. [Ega]
      aren't/isn't allowed to ...
      [Ega] have/has to [qavsdagi].


⚠ 'A CLOAKROOM':

  = garderob (kiyim, sumka
  qoldiriladigan joy).


⚠ 'A SUIT AND TIE':

  = kostyum va galstuk.


⚠ 'A PUBLIC PHONE':

  = jamoat telefoni (taksofon).

items.question: SA: Can I park my car here?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to park here. You have to park somewhere else.

items.prompt: bolani kasalxonaga olib kirish / tashqarida qoldirish
items.question: SA: Can my child come into the hospital?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. He isn't allowed to come in. You have to leave him outside.

items.prompt: muzeyda surat olish / fotoapparatni garderobda qoldirish
items.question: SA: Can we take photographs in the museum?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to take photographs. You have to leave your cameras in the cloakroom.

items.question: SA: Can we eat in here?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to eat in here. You have to eat your food outside.

items.question: SA: Can I wear shorts in this restaurant?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to wear shorts. You have to wear a suit and tie.
items.whyUz: ⚠ 'a suit and tie' = kostyum va galstuk.

items.question: SA: Can I use this telephone?
items.answer: SB: No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to use this telephone. You have to use the public phone outside.

exercises.instructionEn: Had to/didn't have to - Could/couldn't — Use
exercises.instructionUz: Had to/didn't have to - Could/couldn't — Ishlatilishi
exercises.explanationUz:
O'TGAN ZAMONDA MAJBURIYaT VA RUXSAT.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  HAD TO / DIDN'T HAVE TO         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = 'have to' / 'don't have to'
  ning O'TGAN ZAMONI.

  'When my father was a boy, he HAD
   TO wear shorts to school.'
  "Children DIDN'T HAVE TO learn
   about computers twenty years
   ago."

  ⚠ 'must' ning o'tgan zamoni YO'Q -
  'had to' ishlatiladi!


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  COULD / COULDN'T                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  = 'can' / 'can't' ning O'TGAN
  ZAMONI (ruxsat, imkoniyat).

  'I COULD go to parties when I was
   17, but I COULDN'T go on my own;
   I HAD TO go with my brother.'


⚠ SAVOL ShAKLLARI:

  DID you HAVE TO ...?
  COULD you ...?


⚠ 'ON MY OWN':

  = yolg'iz o'zim.
  ⚠ 'by myself' bilan bir xil.


⚠ 'TWENTY YEARS AGO':

  = yigirma yil oldin.
  ⚠ 'ago' - vaqtdan KEYIN.

points.en: Had to and didn't have to are the past forms of have to and don't have to.
points.uz: 'had to' va 'didn't have to' - 'have to' va 'don't have to' ning o'tgan zamon shakllari.

points.en: When my father was a boy, he had to wear shorts to school. Children didn't have to learn about computers at school twenty years ago.
points.uz: Otam bola bo'lganida maktabga shortik kiyishi kerak edi. Yigirma yil oldin bolalar maktabda kompyuterni o'rganishi shart emas edi.

points.en: Could and couldn't are the past forms of can and can't.
points.uz: 'could' va 'couldn't' - 'can' va 'can't' ning o'tgan zamon shakllari.

points.en: I could go to parties when I was 17, but I couldn't go on my own; I had to go with my brother.
points.uz: 17 yoshimda ziyofatlarga bora olardim, lekin yolg'iz borolmasdim; akam bilan borishim kerak edi.
points.noteUz:
⚠ 'on my own' = yolg'iz o'zim.
⚠ Uch shakl bir gapda.

exercises.instructionEn: Mrs Smith is telling her granddaughter about her parents' dinner parties when she and her sister were children. Listen and tick (✓) the correct column.
exercises.instructionUz: Smit xonim nabirasiga u va singlisi bola bo'lganida ota-onasining kechki ziyofatlari haqida gapirib beryapti. Tinglang va to'g'ri ustunga ✓ qo'ying.
exercises.explanationUz:
⚠ AUDIO KERAK - jadval yozuvdan
to'ldiriladi.


JADVAL (could / couldn't / had to /
didn't have to):

  wear best clothes - HAD TO
     (namunada tayyor)
  play piano for guests before
     dinner - ?
  cook - ?
  sit at same table as adults - ?
  put elbows on table - ?
  drink wine like adults - ?
  go to bed early - ?
  sit in living room with adults
     after dinner - ?


⚠ EhTIMOLIY (eski davr qoidalari):

  cook → didn't have to
  sit at same table → couldn't
  put elbows on table → couldn't
  drink wine → couldn't
  go to bed early → had to
  ⚠ Audio bilan tekshiring!


⚠ 'A DINNER PARTY':

  = kechki ziyofat (uyda).


⚠ 'ELBOWS':

  = tirsaklar.
  ⚠ 'Don't put your elbows on the
  table!' - odob qoidasi.


⚠ 'A GRANDDAUGHTER':

  = nabira (qiz).

points.uz: eng yaxshi kiyimlarini kiymoq → kerak edi
points.noteUz:
⚠ Namunada tayyor: 'They had to wear their best
clothes.'

points.en: play piano for guests before dinner
sit at same table as adults
sit in living room with adults after dinner
points.uz: ovqatdan keyin kattalar bilan mehmonxonada o'tirmoq

exercises.instructionEn: Finally, ask and answer questions in pairs, using Did they have to...?/Could they ...? as in the example.
exercises.instructionUz: Nihoyat, juftlikda 'Did they have to...?' / 'Could they ...?' bilan savol-javob qiling, namunadagidek.
exercises.explanationUz:
KITOBDAGI NAMUNA:

  SA: Did they have to wear their
      best clothes?
  SB: Yes, they did. They had to
      wear their best clothes.


⚠ SAVOL VA JAVOB QOLIPLARI:

  Did they have to ...?
     Yes, they did. / No, they
     didn't. They didn't have to ...
  Could they ...?
     Yes, they could. / No, they
     couldn't.

⚠ Javoblar audioga bog'liq -
qoliplar berilgan.

items.question: SA: Did they have to wear their best clothes?
items.answer: SB: Yes, they did. They had to wear their best clothes.

items.question: SA: Did they have to play the piano for guests before dinner?
items.answer: SB: Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.

items.question: SA: Could they sit at the same table as adults?
items.answer: SB: Yes, they could. / No, they couldn't.

items.question: SA: Could they put their elbows on the table?
SA: Did they have to go to bed early?
items.answer: SB: Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.

patterns.formula: Can I ...? - No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to ... You have to ...
patterns.exampleEn: Can I park my car here? - No, I'm afraid not. You aren't allowed to park here. You have to park somewhere else.
patterns.exampleUz: Mashinani shu yerga qo'ysam bo'ladimi? - Afsuski, yo'q. Bu yerga qo'yish mumkin emas. Boshqa joyga qo'yishingiz kerak.

patterns.formula: When [kim] was [yosh], [kim] had to / couldn't + FE'L.
patterns.exampleEn: When my father was a boy, he had to wear shorts to school.
patterns.exampleUz: Otam bola bo'lganida maktabga shortik kiyishi kerak edi.

patterns.formula: Did they have to ...? - Yes, they did. / Could they ...? - No, they couldn't.
patterns.exampleEn: Did they have to wear their best clothes? - Yes, they did.
patterns.exampleUz: Ular eng yaxshi kiyimlarini kiyishi kerakmidi? - Ha.

patterns.formula: Taxi drivers must / mustn't / don't have to + FE'L.
patterns.exampleEn: Taxi drivers mustn't be rude to passengers.
patterns.exampleUz: Taksi haydovchilari yo'lovchilarga qo'pol bo'lmasligi shart.
